clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old man with no prior pathological history presented with a one-month history of progressively worsening headaches resistant to analgesics with no neurological deficits on examination. Brain MRI identified a left temporo-parieto-occipital intraaxial tumor causing sub-falcial and temporal herniation, initially suggestive of a high-grade glioma. Histopathological and immunohistochemical confirmation of the tumor as grade III hemangiopericytoma per WHO 2016 classification was documented but source excerpts confirming these details were not provided. Clinical course and treatment details remain undocumented.
